verdict.rationale: Typesense Cloud documents a dedicated-cluster model with "no limits on records or operations", so there are no per-request or per-record cliffs, and the open-source engine can be self-hosted free forever. However, the evidence does not document how cluster pricing scales as data grows. Community reports note the engine is in-memory and needs a lot of RAM, which implies costs rise with dataset size through server sizing. Missing for 10: documented cluster price tiers and how cost scales with RAM or record growth, any independent evidence of cost predictability at scale, and confirmation that higher query volume needs no upsizing.

support.subject: As a founder, costs stay predictable as records and query volume grow — no surprise per-request cliffs

citations.quote: You get a dedicated cluster, with no limits on records or operations.
Self-host it free forever or run the same engine in a dedicated Typesense Cloud cluster.
